metadata.title: Likelihood-Ranked Synthetic Selection in Self-Consuming Diffusion: Minority Extinction Ordering at Moderate Imbalance
metadata.description:
Self-consuming training loops can induce model collapse. We study unlabeled likelihood ranking of synthetic samples in self-consuming DDPM training, emphasizing moderate imbalance. Define the minority-mass ratio r = m(1)/m(0). Results are stratified by imbalance ρ. At ρ=5 (n=5), bottom-k > random-k > top-k on all seeds, with large paired effect sizes (Cohen dz ≈ −1.96 / +1.65); exact Wilcoxon p=0.0625 (minimum attainable at n=5 when all signs agree). At ρ=10 (n=3), the full order holds on 0/3 seeds and contrasts are near null. Top-k does not improve sliced W2 vs random-k at generation 1 (ΔW2>0 on 8/8 cells; exact p=0.0078; Holm-adjusted p=0.039 across five generations). Directional transfers (8D GMM and Digits-PCA; n=3) match the ρ=5 ordering.

Code: https://github.com/muhammadalamzeb/likelihood-rank-self-consuming-diffusion
metadata.notes: Empirical short preprint / workshop-scope note. Primary analysis is stratified by imbalance rho. Exact Wilcoxon signed-rank tests used throughout.
